$comment: RESERVED FOR RUNTIME VALIDATION (JSON Schema cannot enforce these): recomputation of every digest against the actual referenced artifact bytes; verification that a source artifact is genuinely authenticated host evidence before any field may be treated as class C (a SHA-256 digest alone never creates class-C evidence and never establishes factual truth); distinction between operator_attested fields (whose source_ref must resolve to the attestation artifact) and operator_recorded fields (whose source_ref must resolve to a contemporaneous record created at action time); cross-artifact binding of opaque_slot_id and attempt_number across observation, attestation, action log, and captures; temporal ordering of recorded/invoked/completed timestamps; agreement of returned_output_count with actual artifacts; and confirmation that model_reports never replace or shadow observations. A runtime validator must reject artifacts failing any of these even if they satisfy this schema.
title: EXP-019 v1.2 DRAFT operator observation artifact (non-executable)
description: DRAFT schema for the prospective EXP-019 v1.2 evidence contract. This document is NOT a frozen protocol and NOT executable: v1.2 is not registered in frozen_protocol(), and no runtime code reads this schema. It records the proposed operator observation artifact: frozen protocol constants, per-field observations with an explicit source class and observation status, and any optional model-generated report held in a separate namespace. This schema does not authorize an experiment, a generation, a metadata query, or a recovery replay.

status.description: Draft marker. A frozen artifact would carry a different value.

executable.description: False while the schema is a draft. No runtime may consume an artifact with executable=false.

protocol_constants.description: Frozen requested behavior. These are protocol labels, not observations, and carry no observation status.

delivery_mode.description: v1.2 prospective change: exact prompt bytes pasted directly, no file attached to the generation request, and no chat-starter wrapper.

observations.description: Per-field observations. Each field names its authoritative source class and its observation status. A class-D model claim may never occupy an authoritative field.

model_reports.description: Optional, unsolicited model-generated reports. Held in a separate namespace so they can never impersonate authenticated telemetry or overwrite class A/B/C evidence.

claimed_status.description: A model claim may only ever be model_reported.

raw_bytes_base64.description: The original model response bytes, preserved verbatim.

sourceClass.description: A: frozen protocol requirement. B: operator-controlled action, contemporaneous record, or operator attestation. C: authenticated host-observed evidence, if genuinely available. D: model-generated description of events.

authoritativeField.description: A single authoritative observation. Only class B or C evidence may occupy an authoritative field: model_reported is deliberately absent, because a class-D model claim may never occupy an authoritative field and lives only in model_reports. source_ref must be a digest of the supporting artifact for every status other than not_observable or not_applicable. Digest integrity proves the artifact was not altered; it does not establish factual truth and does not by itself establish authenticated class-C evidence.

source_ref.description: Digest of the supporting artifact, or null when the value is not_observable or not_applicable.

source_class.description: An unavailable observation is a statement about authoritative (class B/C) evidence. It may not be labelled class A (a protocol constant, not an observation) or class D (a model claim).

value.description: An available observation must carry an actual value; missing telemetry must use not_observable/not_applicable instead.
